column1: # Mapping: EKS course chapter -> course lab
# Format: <chapter> TAB <lab> TAB <status> TAB <title>
#   status = todo -> lab has to be built
#            ready -> lab exists and is linked from the chapter
# INDEPENDENT SET. The course has its own lab set numbered 101+, exactly like the CKA
# course got labs 101-125 next to the untouched older labs. The existing EKS labs 01-04
# are NOT part of the course and MUST NOT be modified: no edits, no renames, no added
# tasks. If a topic is already covered by an old lab, the course still gets its own lab.
# RULE: the test-tube marker in the contents page goes ONLY into a chapter whose own
# course lab already exists. Until a lab is built, its chapter carries no marker.
# Every lab follows the existing EKS lab layout:
#   env.hcl, vpc/, eks_control_plane/, eks_addons/, worker/ with
#   worker/files/{worker.sh,tests.bats,tasks/,solutions/}
# check_result = bats /var/work/tests/tests.bats
# Chapter numbers refer to tasks/eks/course/README_RU.md (48 chapters).

column4: Cluster as code: VPC, control plane, managed node group, kubeconfig
Cluster access: IAM to RBAC, access entries and access policies
IP address planning: ENI limits, prefix delegation, secondary CIDR
Workload identity: IRSA and Pod Identity for an app reading S3 and Secrets Manager
Secrets: External Secrets with Secrets Manager, KMS envelope encryption
EBS CSI: StatefulSet on gp3, volume expansion, snapshot - MUST include the Immediate versus WaitForFirstConsumer failure and fix (see .content-notes.md)
EFS CSI: ReadWriteMany across AZ
AWS Load Balancer Controller: NLB for a Service of type LoadBalancer
ALB Ingress with ACM certificate, external-dns and Route 53
NetworkPolicy in EKS: built-in VPC CNI network policy (eBPF), default deny, label and namespace rules, egress (see .content-notes.md)
Spot nodes: diversification, interruption handling, graceful drain
Fargate profiles: what runs there, what breaks, cost comparison
Cluster upgrade and rollback: control plane, node groups, addons, deprecated API check, version rollback within the 7 day window
Observability: Container Insights and Managed Prometheus with Grafana
Logging: Fluent Bit to CloudWatch Logs, filtering and retention
Hardening: IMDSv2 hop limit, Pod Security Admission, private endpoint
Traffic cost and egress control: NAT versus VPC endpoints, OpenCost report
GitOps: Argo CD driving the cluster from git
Troubleshooting: node does not reach Ready (IAM, SG, user data, kubelet)
Troubleshooting: broken networking and unhealthy load balancer targets
Troubleshooting: access denied (access entries, IRSA, webhook, kubeconfig)
AWS Backup for EKS: on-demand backup of cluster state and EBS volumes, namespace restore, restore into a second cluster
Karpenter: NodePool, EC2NodeClass, consolidation, drift, plus safe eviction of StatefulSet - PDB, karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt, NodePool disruption budgets (see .content-notes.md)
Application autoscaling: HPA on external metrics, KEDA with a Prometheus trigger, load generator
EKS Auto Mode versus own stack: enable Auto Mode, default NodePools, no SSH or SSM on nodes, 21 day node lifetime, custom NodePool, where the own stack wins (see .content-notes.md)

# NOTE on chapters 41-42 (AWS Backup for EKS). Lab prerequisites, taken from
# https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/eks-backups.html :
#   - cluster authentication mode must be API or API_AND_CONFIG_MAP, AWS Backup
#     creates its own access entry
#   - backup role: AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup, restore role:
#     AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForRestores
#   - EBS CSI addon must be installed on the restore target
#   - restores are non-destructive, existing objects are never overwritten, so the
#     lab has to delete the namespace (or restore into a second cluster) to show it
#   - not supported: in-tree volumes and CSI migration, FSx via CSI, S3 prefixes,
#     cross-account EFS, EFS non-root subpath mounts, EKS on Outposts
